candidate_state: Abeta42 degrades the Kv4 (Shal) A-type K+ channel pan-neuronally, lowering the current/charge needed for the first action potential
condition: Abeta42 (secreted human peptide, pan-neuronal elav-GAL4)
cell_types_as_reported: all neurons (measured in cultured neurons and in mushroom body neurons of the intact adult brain)
malecns_types: all central brain neurons; strongest evidence in KC*
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold down / reduce spike-frequency-adaptation strength pan-neuronally
c1_rationale: Primary quantitative current-clamp and voltage-clamp data with genotype controls (elav/+ and UAS/+) and a specific genetic rescue (Kv4 restoration), plus independent assay replication of the MB-specific IA loss (10.1016/j.neuroscience.2017.06.008). Direction is NOT consistent across labs: Tabuchi 2015 found no excitability change with Abeta42 in l-LNv neurons (only AbetaArctic did) (10.1016/j.cub.2015.01.016), and Higham 2019 reported DECREASED K+-evoked Ca2+ influx in Kenyon cells expressing Abeta42 (10.3389/fncel.2019.00260). Grade 1 rather than 2 because of this directional conflict and because the ramp/threshold values come from embryo-derived cultures.
c2_rationale: The cellular change was measured directly (Kv4 current density, AP threshold, Kv4 protein) and in the intact adult brain for mushroom body neurons (10.1371/journal.pgen.1005025). Mapping is weak for the pan-neuronal version: the driver is all neurons, so there is no cell-type-specific target; threshold values themselves come from a mixed culture. Grade 1.
c3_rationale: An excitability shift (firing threshold, SFA strength) is an existing operator. No neuromodulation, plasticity rule, metabolism or glia is needed.
notes: Scale target: Ping 2015 reports threshold current 35.9->19.5 pA and charge 5132.8->2197.4 pA*ms, i.e. a ~46% reduction in the current and ~57% reduction in the charge needed for the first spike. Passive properties were unchanged, which supports modelling this as a pure threshold/adaptation change rather than a conductance/leak change.

candidate_state: Abeta42-driven Kv4/IA loss restricted to mushroom body (Kenyon) neurons
condition: Abeta42 (MB-restricted, 201y-GAL4 / OK107-GAL4 expression; IA measured in MB neurons)
cell_types_as_reported: mushroom body neurons (Kenyon cells)
malecns_types: KC* (4064 cells: KCab-s/m/c/p, KCg-m, KCg-d, KCa'b'-ap1/ap2/m)
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold down / reduce SFA strength in KC* only
c1_rationale: Kv4 current density is reduced in GFP-labelled MB neurons in the intact adult brain at 8 days but not 3 days (n=6-13), and IA is reduced in MB neurons but not projection neurons (10.1016/j.neuroscience.2017.06.008), so the cell-type specificity has been tested directly. Only one group, and absolute values are in figures; the opposite direction is reported for Kenyon cells by an independent group using Ca2+ imaging (10.3389/fncel.2019.00260).
c2_rationale: Direct patch-clamp measurement in an identified cell type in the intact adult brain, and Kenyon cells map unambiguously to KC* in MaleCNS v1.0 (cell_class Kenyon_Cell).
c3_rationale: Excitability shift restricted to KC* uses an existing operator.
notes: The model's current memory tasks are visual and do not engage Kenyon cells, so this candidate can be implemented and checked for circuit-level effects (KC output onto MBONs/APL) but has no behavioural readout in the current task set. That is a C5 problem, not a C3 problem.

candidate_state: Intraneuronal Abeta lowers synaptic vesicle release probability, with fewer Ca2+-channel clusters and less Bruchpilot, without bouton loss
condition: Abeta42 / Abeta-Arctic accumulating intraneuronally (A307-GAL4-type expression in identified neurons)
cell_types_as_reported: identified single neuron and its presynaptic terminals (DLM motor neuron of the giant fiber pathway in the same group's related work)
malecns_types: DLMn a,b / DLMn c-f (if the DLM motor neuron); otherwise unassigned
proposed_model_operator: scale presynaptic release strength down; scale active-zone strength down; increase short-term depression
c1_rationale: Primary, directional and age-resolved cellular measurements from one group across two papers of the same model (release probability, Ca2+-channel clusters, Brp, vesicle pools, synaptic fatigue), and consistent in direction with the late-stage decrease in spontaneous transmission that an independent group measured in adult projection neurons (10.1016/j.celrep.2018.06.029). No numbers are stated in the abstracts, no independent lab replication of release probability itself.
c2_rationale: The presynaptic parameter was measured directly, but the recording site is a peripheral neuromuscular synapse of a motor neuron, and the paper's abstract does not name the cell type, so the MaleCNS mapping is low-to-medium confidence and is not a central synapse the model uses.
c3_rationale: Presynaptic release scaling, active-zone strength and short-term-depression parameters are all existing operators.
notes: Quantities to fit are not published as numbers; the calibration entry therefore carries a direction and a free parameter, not a published percentage.

candidate_state: Late-stage Abeta42 expression removes neurons (Kenyon cells first, then other regions; photoreceptors in the eye)
condition: Abeta42 (pan-neuronal or MB-restricted), 25-50 days after eclosion
cell_types_as_reported: mushroom body neurons / Kenyon cell layer; photoreceptors (Rh1-GAL4)
malecns_types: KC*; R1-R6 and R7* for the retinal model
proposed_model_operator: remove neurons (delete a fraction of KC* cells; delete a fraction of R1-R6)
c1_rationale: Multiple independent labs, consistent direction and timing: ~17% fewer MB neurons at 40 days with MB-restricted Abeta42 (132.10+/-3.17 -> 110.30+/-4.03, n=8-9 brains; 10.1371/journal.pgen.1005025), vacuolar loss in the Kenyon cell layer from 30 days (10.1073/pnas.0400895101), doubled vacuole number at 2 weeks with adult-onset expression (10.1016/j.celrep.2018.11.098), and 92% -> 56% of ommatidia with intact rhabdomeres at 30 days (10.1186/s40478-016-0333-4). Rescue (Kv4) and modifier (azot) experiments support causality.
c2_rationale: Cell counts are the measurement, and both Kenyon cells and photoreceptors map with high confidence onto MaleCNS types (KC*, R1-R6/R7*).
c3_rationale: Neuron removal is a core operator.
notes: The retinal variant is the most useful one for this model because the current memory tasks are visual: deleting a graded fraction of R1-R6 gives a dose-response curve that can be compared with the published 56%/92% rhabdomere survival.

candidate_state: Human or fly tau accumulating in Kenyon cells impairs learning; MB neurons show reduced depolarisation-evoked Ca2+ influx before any degeneration
condition: human tau (0N4R, 0N3R), bovine tau, Drosophila tau; MB drivers (c492, c772, OK107, LeoMB)
cell_types_as_reported: adult mushroom body neurons (Kenyon cells)
malecns_types: KC*
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold up / increase SFA strength in KC* (reduced excitability)
c1_rationale: Behavioural evidence is strong and replicated: 25-30% learning impairment with three different tau proteins and two MB drivers plus proper heterozygote controls (10.1101/lm.70804), 1-h memory abolished by MB tau (10.3389/fncel.2019.00409). But an adult-onset, MB-restricted experiment with ~14-fold higher tau found NO protein-synthesis-dependent memory deficit (31.915+/-2.564 vs 37.573+/-3.367, p=0.2306; 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.1374-22.2023), so the behavioural consequence of tau in Kenyon cells depends on isoform, aggregation state and training protocol. Cellular evidence (48.1% reduced Ca2+ influx) comes from one group.
c2_rationale: A representable cellular parameter was measured directly in the right cell type (peak K+-evoked Ca2+ influx in MB lobes, 48.1% reduction, p=0.006; 10.3389/fncel.2019.00409), and KC* maps with high confidence. Grade 1 because a bulk Ca2+ response is an indirect proxy for excitability and the measurement is single-lab.
c3_rationale: A reduction in excitability of KC* is an existing operator (threshold up / stronger adaptation).
notes: Direction is opposite to the Abeta42/Kv4 candidate even though both are reported in Kenyon cells. The two should be implemented as separate, oppositely signed states and not merged.

candidate_state: Adult-onset pan-neuronal human tau impairs learning rate and protein-synthesis-dependent memory, reversibly, with protein-synthesis-independent memory spared
condition: human tau 0N4R, adult-specific pan-neuronal (ElavGAL4;GAL80ts), 12 days at 30 C
cell_types_as_reported: all CNS neurons
malecns_types: pan-neuronal
proposed_model_operator: none available (the measured mechanism is translation/plasticity-dependent memory, not a synaptic or excitability parameter)
c1_rationale: Best-quantified fly dataset in this review: learning 50.609+/-1.981 vs 65.831+/-1.020 and 67.671+/-1.432 (p=5.03e-6, 9.00e-9, n>=12), PSD-M 16.473+/-1.656 vs 26.506+/-2.482 (p=0.0089), PSI-M unaffected, full reversal on transgene repression (32.962+/-2.346 vs 22.034+/-1.548, p=0.0015), all confirmed with an independent site-specific double transgene.
c2_rationale: No representable cellular parameter was measured. The paper's mechanism is the solubility/aggregation state of tau and its effect on protein-synthesis-dependent memory; the only electrophysiology for pan-neuronal tau is from a different study and circuit (giant fiber conduction and failure rate, 10.1016/j.nbd.2018.12.004), which is a separate candidate.
c3_rationale: Protein-synthesis-dependent memory requires a plasticity rule and translation, both explicitly outside the model. Nothing in the paper specifies a weight, release or threshold change to implement.
notes: Keep as the reference behavioural dataset for what a tauopathy phenotype looks like, and as a reminder that the reversibility argues against modelling tau as cell death.

candidate_state: Aging enlarges presynaptic active-zone scaffolds (T-bar size, BRP/RBP content) and increases odour-evoked vesicle release at PN-to-Kenyon-cell synapses, while active-zone number per bouton falls and postsynaptic Ca2+ does not rise
condition: normal aging (3 days vs 30 days), suppressed by spermidine
cell_types_as_reported: projection neuron boutons in the mushroom body calyx; Kenyon cell axons and dendritic claws
malecns_types: ALPN -> KC* (686 ALPN cells; 4064 KC cells)
proposed_model_operator: scale active-zone strength up and presynaptic release strength up for ALPN->KC* (plus stronger short-term depression); optionally reduce the number of ALPN->KC* synapses per connection
c1_rationale: Converging measurements of the same change by EM, STED, immuno-EM and SynaptopHluorin in one paper (10.1371/journal.pbio.1002563), with spermidine suppression in two papers (10.1038/nn.3512), a causality test by BRP gene dosage (4xBRP young flies perform like 30-day-old controls), an independent-circuit replication at the adult NMJ (10.1002/cne.23798), and follow-up work establishing the same brain-wide 'PreScale' signature (10.1371/journal.pbio.3001730; 10.1038/s41467-019-09262-2).
c2_rationale: The synaptic parameter itself (T-bar size, BRP amount, vesicle release) was measured at an identified, named synapse (PN-to-KC in the calyx), and both partners map with high confidence onto ALPN and KC*.
c3_rationale: Active-zone strength scaling, presynaptic release scaling and short-term-depression parameters are all existing operators; no plasticity rule is needed because the published manipulation (BRP dosage) is itself a static scaling.
notes: All numbers are in figures/S1 Data, so the calibration entry must carry a direction and a fitted magnitude. Note the two opposing components: release goes up while active-zone number per bouton goes down, and postsynaptic Ca2+ does not increase, so an implementation that only raises release strength will overshoot the postsynaptic effect.

candidate_state: Aging reduces DPM-to-alpha/beta-Kenyon-cell contacts specifically at the alpha-lobe tip, abolishing the DPM ITM trace and the alpha/beta LTM trace
condition: normal aging (10 days vs 30 days)
cell_types_as_reported: dorsal paired medial (DPM) neurons and alpha/beta mushroom body neurons
malecns_types: DPM (2 cells, annotated dopaminergic in MaleCNS) -> KCab-s/m/c/p
proposed_model_operator: remove DPM->KC connections (synapse removal) -- but see C3
c1_rationale: Two papers from the same group with consistent, compartment-specific results: ITM trace lost at 30 days with the alpha'/beta' STM trace spared (10.1073/pnas.1118126109), LTM trace lost, GRASP contacts reduced selectively at the alpha tip, DPM morphology unchanged, and a loss of the DPM synaptic-output requirement in aged flies, confirmed with two independent DPM drivers (10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0978-14.2015). Causality supported by the 40% ITM rescue when DPM excitability is raised (p=0.019).
c2_rationale: Both partners map uniquely (DPM is a single pair, KCab* are well defined), and the connectivity change was measured directly, but GRASP intensity is a proxy for contact number rather than a synapse count, and no numbers are published.
c3_rationale: Synapse removal is an available operator, but in this model the two DPM neurons are annotated dopaminergic and dopamine synapses carry zero weight, so deleting DPM->KC connections changes nothing. The published rescue (raising DPM excitability with TrpM8/TrpA1) is equally silent for the same reason. The DPM mechanism also involves the amnesiac neuropeptide and serotonin, neither of which the model carries.
notes: Revisit if the model ever gives DPM a non-zero weight. If DPM is re-annotated (its transmitter identity is debated in the literature - serotonin and the amnesiac neuropeptide have both been proposed), this becomes a strong candidate immediately.

candidate_state: PD-like dopaminergic dysfunction: alpha-synuclein in PAM neurons reduces their connections to Kenyon cells; parkin/PINK1 loss causes dopaminergic synapse loss and reduced dopamine release; progressive locomotor decline
condition: alpha-synuclein, parkin, PINK1
cell_types_as_reported: PAM cluster (15 DA neurons per hemisphere innervating beta/beta' lobes), PPL1/PPM/PAL clusters
malecns_types: PAM01-PAM15 (316 cells), PPL101-PPL108, PPM1201-PPM1205, PAL01/PAL03 - all annotated dopaminergic
proposed_model_operator: remove neurons and/or remove synapses from dopaminergic clusters -- but see C3
c1_rationale: Many labs, consistent behaviour (progressive climbing decline), but the cellular claim is contested: whole-mount counting found no dopaminergic cell loss with alpha-synuclein (10.1002/gene.20106), aged wild-type flies lose no dopaminergic neurons at all (10.3389/fnins.2010.00205), and synaptic/presynaptic loss precedes any cell loss (10.1016/j.celrep.2013.10.032; 10.1093/braincomms/fcab049). Grade 1 for inconsistent cellular direction and magnitudes that are never published as counts for the affected clusters.
c2_rationale: The dopaminergic clusters map cleanly onto MaleCNS DAN types, and the PAM-to-Kenyon-cell connection is explicitly named (10.1016/j.celrep.2013.10.032), but the published measures are reporter intensity, voltammetric release and TH counts rather than a synapse count, and the key full text was not accessible (abstract only).
c3_rationale: Removing the neurons or their synapses is an available operator, but dopaminergic synapses carry zero weight in this model, so the manipulation is functionally silent. The measured mechanism (dopamine release, dopamine receptor levels) is neuromodulation, which the model explicitly does not represent.
notes: Can still be used as a structural null test: deleting all 395 dopaminergic cells should leave the healthy-model readouts unchanged, which is a useful C4/C6 sanity check of the zero-weight assumption.

candidate_state: dfmr1 null mutants have reduced 5-HT2A receptor levels in the mushroom body circuit, and 5-HT2AR knockdown phenocopies the learning/memory deficit
condition: dfmr1 (fragile X) null, adults 7-9 days post-eclosion
cell_types_as_reported: mushroom body alpha', beta' and gamma lobes
malecns_types: KC* (receptor level, not a synapse)
proposed_model_operator: none available (serotonin receptor signalling)
c1_rationale: Quantitative imaging and behaviour with background and transgene controls, p values throughout, phenocopy by 5-HT2AR RNAi, rescue by 5-HT2AR overexpression and by two independent routes of raising serotonin (Trhn overexpression, SERT knockdown), and consistent results in trained and untrained animals (10.1038/s41598-025-34492-4). Only one paper, so no independent replication yet.
c2_rationale: The cellular change was measured directly (receptor immunofluorescence in identified MB lobes) and the lobes map onto KC* with high confidence, but the measured quantity is a postsynaptic receptor level for a modulator, not a parameter the model carries.
c3_rationale: Serotonergic synapses carry zero weight in the model and there is no receptor-level operator. Scaling an excitatory or inhibitory weight would not be the published mechanism.
notes: The same paper's behavioural dataset is still useful as the phenotype target for the other fragile X candidate (C13), which does have a representable mechanism.

candidate_state: Early Abeta42 raises spontaneous synaptic transmission onto adult antennal lobe projection neurons (presynaptic, Dalpha7-dependent)
condition: Abeta42, 0-2 days after eclosion
cell_types_as_reported: antennal lobe projection neurons (PNs) in the intact adult brain
malecns_types: ALPN (686 cells); presynaptic partners ORN_* and ALLN
proposed_model_operator: scale presynaptic release strength up for inputs onto ALPN
c1_rationale: Primary patch-clamp data in an identified adult cell type with explicit values and n (5579.67+/-1804.34 -> 2439.60+/-1182.44 ms, n=7/9, p<0.05) and a presynaptic localisation of the effect from mEPSC frequency with unchanged amplitude, confirmed with two independent Abeta42 lines in culture (10.1016/j.celrep.2018.06.029). One group only, and an independent study of pupal projection neurons reported the opposite sign (decreased mEPSC frequency; 10.1007/s12264-012-1267-x), although at a different developmental stage.
c2_rationale: Directly measured presynaptic release parameter in an identified adult cell type; ALPN maps with high confidence (cell_class ALPN).
c3_rationale: Presynaptic release scaling is an existing operator.
notes: Caveat for implementation: the measurement is of events arriving at the PN, so the scaling belongs on the ORN->ALPN (and ALLN->ALPN) connections, not on ALPN output.

candidate_state: At 9-13 days, Abeta42 depresses spontaneous transmission onto adult projection neurons (homeostatic reversal of the early increase)
condition: Abeta42, 9-13 days after eclosion
cell_types_as_reported: antennal lobe projection neurons (PNs)
malecns_types: ALPN; presynaptic ORN_*, ALLN
proposed_model_operator: scale presynaptic release strength down for inputs onto ALPN
c1_rationale: Same study, same cell type, explicit values (1256.57+/-263.68 -> 2161.49+/-624.18 ms, +70%, n=6/8, p<0.05) with two independent lines in culture, and the direction agrees with independently reported late-stage presynaptic weakening (10.1016/j.nbd.2012.11.006). Single group for the adult measurement.
c2_rationale: Direct presynaptic measurement in an identified adult cell type that maps to ALPN with high confidence.
c3_rationale: Presynaptic release scaling is an existing operator.
notes: The sign flip between C11 and C12 is itself the interesting prediction: an age-staged pair of simulations (early up, late down) is the faithful representation, not a single static change. The published cause of the reversal is homeostatic plasticity, which the model cannot generate on its own - so the two states must be imposed, not derived.

candidate_state: dfmr1 null weakens GABAergic lateral inhibition from antennal lobe local interneurons onto projection neurons, broadening odour tuning
condition: dfmr1 (fragile X) null, adult
cell_types_as_reported: antennal lobe GABAergic local interneurons (LNs) and projection neurons (PNs)
malecns_types: ALLN (420 cells, GABAergic) -> ALPN (686 cells)
proposed_model_operator: scale presynaptic release strength down on ALLN->ALPN connections (and ALLN->ALLN); optionally remove a fraction of those synapses
c1_rationale: Direct in vivo patch-clamp with optogenetic activation of the identified presynaptic population, matched n (16 vs 16 PNs; 8 vs 16 LNs), explicit p values (LN depolarisation p=6.5e-4; tuning sparseness p=9.8e-14), a genomic rescue of the behaviour, and a mechanism test showing the deficit is not secondary to ChR2 expression (10.1016/j.cub.2017.02.065). Direction agrees with independent reports of GABAergic dysfunction in the same model (10.1016/j.nbd.2014.01.008).
c2_rationale: The synaptic parameter (strength of inhibition from a named presynaptic class onto a named postsynaptic class) was measured directly, and both classes map with high confidence onto MaleCNS ALLN and ALPN. GABA is not one of the zero-weight transmitters in this model.
c3_rationale: Scaling presynaptic release on an identified inhibitory connection, or removing a fraction of those synapses, are both existing operators.
notes: Also the cleanest circuit-level prediction to check: weaker ALLN->ALPN inhibition should broaden ALPN tuning in the model, which is a direct analogue of the published lifetime-sparseness result.

candidate_state: Aging reduces brain KCNQ (M-current) expression to about 10% of young levels, and KCNQ loss in mushroom body alpha/beta neurons reproduces age-related memory impairment
condition: normal aging (1-5 days vs 25-30 days)
cell_types_as_reported: adult brain (mRNA); mushroom body alpha/beta neurons (behavioural requirement and rescue)
malecns_types: KCab-s, KCab-m, KCab-c, KCab-p
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold down / reduce SFA strength in KCab* (loss of a slow adaptation current)
c1_rationale: Quantitative expression decline (to ~10% of the 5-day level, p<0.05), a null mutant that phenocopies aged memory, a precise-excision genetic control, and MB-restricted rescue of age-related memory impairment (10.1371/journal.pone.0062445). But the aged-fly excitability change itself was not recorded; the excitability direction is inferred from separate KCNQ-RNAi/overexpression experiments.
c2_rationale: The MB alpha/beta requirement is established genetically and maps to KCab*, but the measurement in aged animals is mRNA level, not a current or a firing rate, so the link to a model parameter is one inference step removed.
c3_rationale: An M-current/afterhyperpolarisation loss maps directly onto the model's spike-frequency-adaptation strength and threshold operators.
notes: Interesting because it predicts aged Kenyon cells should be MORE excitable, while Gupta 2016 reports reduced postsynaptic Ca2+ responses in aged Kenyon cell dendrites. A simulation can test whether both can hold at once.

candidate_state: Human tau in the M4/M6 mushroom body output neurons raises depolarisation-evoked Ca2+ influx about 2.7-fold via more L-type Ca2+ channels
condition: human tau 0N4R, R21D02-GAL4, 2-5 day old adults
cell_types_as_reported: MB output neurons M4/M6
malecns_types: MBON01, MBON03, MBON04 (glutamatergic M4/M6 MBONs)
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold down / reduce SFA strength in MBON01/03/04
c1_rationale: Explicit effect size with p value (268.9+/-45.2% of control, p=0.005), a pharmacological identification of the carrier (nimodipine returns it to 98.9+/-21.1%), a transcript measurement in the same direction (Ca-alpha1D +68%, p=0.04), and a behavioural rescue by knocking the channel down. Single paper, single lab; the companion paper reports the opposite sign in Kenyon cells, so cell-type specificity is essential and untested elsewhere.
c2_rationale: Directly measured in identified MBONs; M4/M6 corresponds to the glutamatergic MBON01/MBON03/MBON04 types in MaleCNS (mapping confidence medium-high because R21D02 covers more than one MBON).
c3_rationale: An excitability shift restricted to named MBON types is an existing operator.
notes: Pairs with C16 (opposite sign in Kenyon cells) from the same group; the two together make a testable prediction about the KC->MBON transformation.

candidate_state: Human tau (and Abeta42) in Kenyon cells reduces depolarisation-evoked Ca2+ influx by about 48% before any degeneration
condition: human tau 0N4R or Abeta42, OK107-GAL4, 2-5 day old adults
cell_types_as_reported: mushroom body neurons (whole MB lobes)
malecns_types: KC*
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold up / increase SFA strength in KC*
c1_rationale: Explicit effect size with p value (48.1% reduction, p=0.006) and the same direction for Abeta42, tau and Ank2 knockdown in a companion paper with intact MB lobes verified by imaging. Both papers are from one group, and the direction conflicts with the Kv4-loss hyperexcitability account (10.1371/journal.pgen.1005025).
c2_rationale: Measured directly in KC*, which map with high confidence; the readout is a bulk lobe Ca2+ response rather than single-cell firing.
c3_rationale: Excitability shift in KC* is an existing operator.
notes: Implement as the explicit alternative hypothesis to C02. A robustness check (C6) that sweeps KC excitability in both directions is the efficient way to handle the contradiction in the literature.

candidate_state: Human tau isoforms raise response failure rate at high-frequency stimulation (0N3R) and slow conduction (0N4R) in the adult giant fiber system
condition: human tau 0N3R / 0N4R / 0N4R-R406W, adult, age-dependent
cell_types_as_reported: giant fiber system: giant fiber, peripherally synapsing interneuron, TTM and DLM motor neurons
malecns_types: DNp01, PSI, TTMn, DLMn a,b / DLMn c-f, GFC1-GFC4
proposed_model_operator: increase short-term depression (raise failure rate) at the identified cholinergic synapse; optionally scale presynaptic release down
c1_rationale: Isoform-resolved electrophysiology in an identified adult circuit with an internal expression control (0N4R vs R406W expressed equivalently), and the same circuit shows the same kind of failure with normal aging (130 Hz at 5 days falling to 60-80 Hz at 35-45 days; 10.1002/dneu.20388) and with Abeta (10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3699-09.2010). Only abstracts were accessible for the tau paper, so no values are recorded.
c2_rationale: The measured quantity (failure rate under repeated stimulation) is exactly a short-term-depression parameter, and the circuit's components exist as MaleCNS types, but the paper's 'specific cholinergic synapse' is not identified as a MaleCNS connection, so the mapping is medium confidence.
c3_rationale: Short-term-depression parameters and presynaptic scaling are existing operators.
overall: PASS C1-C3 (shortlist, values pending full text)
notes: Needs the full text of 10.1016/j.nbd.2018.12.004 (and 10.1002/dneu.20388) before any number can be fitted; the failure-rate measure is the closest thing in this literature to a directly fittable short-term-depression parameter.

candidate_state: Intraneuronal Abeta accelerates age-dependent synaptic fatigue at 100 Hz in an identified motor neuron, with fewer vesicles and depleted presynaptic mitochondria
condition: Abeta42 x2 / Abeta-Arctic, A307-GAL4, 9-21 days
cell_types_as_reported: DLM motor neuron of the giant fiber pathway
malecns_types: DLMn a,b / DLMn c-f (and the upstream DNp01/PSI pathway)
proposed_model_operator: increase short-term depression; scale presynaptic release down; scale active-zone strength down
c1_rationale: Longitudinal, dose-ordered (Arctic > Abeta42x2 > control) measurements in an identified adult neuron with an ultrastructural correlate, and a frequency control (no age effect at 10 Hz) that argues the change is a use-dependent release defect rather than general decline. One group; values in figures only.
c2_rationale: Direct measurement of a short-term-depression parameter in an identified neuron, but at a peripheral neuromuscular synapse that the model does not contain; only the upstream central pathway is in MaleCNS.
c3_rationale: Short-term-depression parameters, presynaptic scaling and active-zone scaling are existing operators.
notes: Most useful as the mechanistic companion to C03 (same group, same model): fatigue is the functional read-out of the reduced release probability.

candidate_state: Sleep deprivation raises l-LNv firing about 1.8-fold and compounds AbetaArctic-induced hyperexcitability, with reduced KCa and IA at spike threshold
condition: sleep loss alone and combined with AbetaArctic (cry-GAL4)
cell_types_as_reported: large ventral lateral clock neurons (l-LNv)
malecns_types: l-LNv (8 cells; annotated serotonin in MaleCNS)
proposed_model_operator: shift firing threshold down / reduce SFA strength in l-LNv -- but see C3
c1_rationale: Whole-cell recordings with pharmacological isolation of the cells, spontaneous and evoked measures agreeing, the specific currents identified, a pharmacological rescue (levetiracetam) that also extends lifespan, and an independent report of elevated l-LNv firing with tau in the same neurons (10.1016/j.nbd.2019.104507). Important caveat recorded in the atlas: Abeta42 and Abeta40 alone did NOT change excitability in these cells - only the Arctic variant did.
c2_rationale: Direct current-clamp measurement in a uniquely identifiable cell type that exists as a MaleCNS type (l-LNv, 8 cells).
c3_rationale: The operator exists (threshold shift), but in this model l-LNv is annotated serotonergic, so whatever firing change is imposed cannot propagate: the cells' outgoing weights are zero. The state is representable in the cell but not in the circuit.
overall: FAIL C3 (operator available, effect cannot propagate)
notes: If the model is ever extended so that l-LNv has non-zero output, this becomes the only candidate in the review with a published sleep-loss-by-pathology interaction at the level of single-neuron excitability.

candidate_state: A single sleep deprivation in mid-stage alpha-synuclein flies causes persistent short-term memory loss that requires D1-like receptor activation
condition: alpha-synuclein plus 12 h sleep deprivation at 16 days
cell_types_as_reported: whole animal; dopamine receptor transcripts (dDA1, DAMB); dopaminergic clusters unchanged
malecns_types: n/a (dopaminergic signalling; PPM12*, PPL1* counts unchanged)
proposed_model_operator: none available

c1_rationale: A single 1984 study with no modern replication; no genotype controls in the modern sense, counts reported only as a percentage change in the abstract, and the measure is fibre profiles rather than somata. Later aging work at the same synapses reports changes in active-zone number and size rather than Kenyon cell loss (10.1371/journal.pbio.1002563), and the best-powered modern cell-count study in aging flies found no dopaminergic neuron loss at all (10.3389/fnins.2010.00205), so the premise that normal aging removes central neurons is unsupported.
c2_rationale: Kenyon cells map cleanly, but fibre counts in a sectioned pedunculus are not a cell count and the paper reports no per-type numbers.
c3_rationale: Neuron removal is a core operator.
notes: Do not use as an aging state. Listed so the decision is on record: normal aging in this model should be represented synaptically (C07, C14), not as cell loss.

notes: Unique in this review: it is the only well-quantified pathological state in a cell type the model's existing visual memory tasks actually drive, so it is the natural first implementation and the natural C5 test.

c1_rationale: Primary imaging and histology with a stated temporal order (release loss precedes tangle-like pathology and cell loss) plus a counterintuitive internal control (hyperphosphorylated tauE14 is protective), and an independent voltammetric report of reduced dopamine release in a different PD model (10.1021/acschemneuro.2c00277). notes: Together with C09 and C24 this is the third dopaminergic candidate to fail on the same structural ground; the zero-weight choice, not the literature, is the limiting factor for every PD-like state.
